name: Abigail
reference: 1 Samuel 25:3 — the wise woman who later became David's wife.

name: Adah
reference: Genesis 4:19 — a wife of Lamech.

name: Anna
reference: Luke 2:36 — the elderly prophetess who welcomed the infant Jesus.

name: Bathsheba
reference: 2 Samuel 11:3 — the wife of David and mother of Solomon.

name: Deborah
reference: Judges 4:4 — the prophetess and judge who led Israel.

name: Dinah
reference: Genesis 30:21 — the daughter of Jacob and Leah.

name: Eden
reference: Genesis 2:8 — the garden God planted for the first man and woman.

name: Elisheba
reference: Exodus 6:23 — the wife of Aaron.

name: Esther
reference: Book of Esther — the queen who saved her people.

name: Eve
reference: Genesis 3:20 — the first woman and 'mother of all living'.

name: Hagar
reference: Genesis 16:1 — Sarah's servant, mother of Ishmael, whom God saw in the wilderness.

name: Hannah
reference: 1 Samuel 1:20 — the woman whose prayer for a child was answered with Samuel.

name: Hadassah
reference: Esther 2:7 — the Hebrew name of Queen Esther.

name: Jael
reference: Judges 4:21 — the woman who helped deliver Israel from Sisera.

name: Jemima
reference: Job 42:14 — the first daughter born to Job after his restoration.

name: Jochebed
reference: Exodus 6:20 — the mother of Moses, Aaron and Miriam.

name: Judith
reference: Genesis 26:34 and the Book of Judith (deuterocanonical).

name: Keturah
reference: Genesis 25:1 — a wife of Abraham.

name: Keziah
reference: Job 42:14 — the second daughter born to Job after his restoration.

name: Leah
reference: Genesis 29:16 — the first wife of Jacob and mother of six tribes.

name: Lois
reference: 2 Timothy 1:5 — the grandmother of Timothy, known for her faith.

name: Martha
reference: Luke 10:38 — the sister of Mary and Lazarus who welcomed Jesus into her home.

name: Mary
reference: Luke 1:27 — the mother of Jesus.

name: Miriam
reference: Exodus 15:20 — the prophetess and sister of Moses.

name: Naomi
reference: Ruth 1:2 — the mother-in-law of Ruth.

name: Rachel
reference: Genesis 29:16 — the beloved wife of Jacob and mother of Joseph and Benjamin.

name: Rebecca
reference: Genesis 24:15 — the wife of Isaac and mother of Jacob and Esau.

name: Rhoda
reference: Acts 12:13 — the servant girl who answered the door when Peter knocked.

name: Ruth
reference: Book of Ruth — the loyal daughter-in-law of Naomi and ancestor of King David.

name: Salome
reference: Mark 15:40 — a woman who followed Jesus and was present at the cross.

name: Sarah
reference: Genesis 17:15 — the wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac.

name: Susanna
reference: Luke 8:3 — one of the women who supported Jesus' ministry.

name: Tamar
reference: Genesis 38:6 — the daughter-in-law of Judah, named in the genealogy of Jesus.

name: Tirzah
reference: Numbers 26:33 — a daughter of Zelophehad.

name: Zipporah
reference: Exodus 2:21 — the wife of Moses.

name: Zillah
reference: Genesis 4:19 — a wife of Lamech.

name: Rahab
reference: Joshua 2:1 — the woman of Jericho praised for her faith in Hebrews 11:31.

name: Hephzibah
reference: Isaiah 62:4 — a name given to Jerusalem to show God's delight.

name: Michal
reference: 1 Samuel 18:20 — the daughter of Saul and wife of David.

name: Naamah
reference: Genesis 4:22 — a sister of Tubal-cain.

name: Shiphrah
reference: Exodus 1:15 — a Hebrew midwife who feared God and saved the baby boys.

name: Mara
reference: Ruth 1:20 — the name Naomi took in her grief.

name: Eunice
reference: 2 Timothy 1:5 — the mother of Timothy, praised for her sincere faith.

name: Priscilla
reference: Acts 18:2 — the coworker of Paul who taught alongside her husband Aquila.

name: Lydia
reference: Acts 16:14 — the seller of purple cloth and first European convert.

name: Phoebe
reference: Romans 16:1 — a servant of the church at Cenchreae commended by Paul.

name: Dorcas
reference: Acts 9:36 — the disciple in Joppa known for her good works.

name: Tabitha
reference: Acts 9:36 — the Aramaic name of Dorcas, raised to life by Peter.

name: Elizabeth
reference: Luke 1:5 — the mother of John the Baptist.

name: Joanna
reference: Luke 8:3 — a follower of Jesus who supported his ministry.

name: Chloe
reference: 1 Corinthians 1:11 — a woman whose household reported news to Paul.

name: Claudia
reference: 2 Timothy 4:21 — a believer who sent greetings through Paul.

name: Julia
reference: Romans 16:15 — a believer greeted by Paul.

name: Junia
reference: Romans 16:7 — a believer Paul called notable among the apostles.

name: Candace
reference: Acts 8:27 — the title of the queen served by the Ethiopian official.

name: Magdalene
reference: Luke 8:2 — Mary Magdalene, the first to see the risen Jesus.

name: Bethany
reference: John 11:1 — the village of Mary, Martha and Lazarus.

name: Maria
reference: Latin form of Mary, the mother of Jesus (Luke 1:27).

name: Bernice
reference: Acts 25:13 — the sister of King Agrippa who heard Paul.

name: Sharon
reference: Song of Solomon 2:1 — 'rose of Sharon', a fertile coastal plain.

name: Carmel
reference: 1 Kings 18:19 — Mount Carmel, where Elijah met the prophets of Baal.

name: Gloria
reference: From 'Gloria in excelsis Deo', the angels' song in Luke 2:14.

name: Susan
reference: An English form of Susanna, the follower of Jesus in Luke 8:3.

name: Anne
reference: Saint Anne, traditionally the mother of the Virgin Mary (not named in the Bible).

name: Isabella
reference: An Italian form of Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist.

name: Lily
reference: The lily is a Christian symbol of purity; Jesus speaks of the lilies of the field in Matthew 6:28.

name: Gabriella
reference: A feminine form of Gabriel, the angel of the Annunciation.

name: Michaela
reference: A feminine form of Michael, the archangel.

name: Danielle
reference: A French feminine form of Daniel, the prophet.

name: Josephine
reference: A feminine form of Joseph; also Saint Josephine Bakhita.

name: Johanna
reference: A Germanic form of Joanna, the follower of Jesus in Luke 8:3.

name: Hope
reference: One of the three Christian virtues named in 1 Corinthians 13:13.

name: Faith
reference: One of the three Christian virtues named in 1 Corinthians 13:13.

name: Grace
reference: A central word of the faith, as in Ephesians 2:8.

name: Charity
reference: The greatest of the Christian virtues in 1 Corinthians 13.

name: Joy
reference: Named among the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22.

name: Mercy
reference: Jesus teaches 'be merciful' in Luke 6:36.

name: Prudence
reference: One of the four classical virtues, often praised in Proverbs.

name: Constance
reference: A virtue name meaning steadfastness, used by many Christian families.

name: Felicity
reference: Saint Felicity, an early martyr who died with Saint Perpetua.

name: Verity
reference: A virtue name recalling John 14:6, 'I am the way, the truth and the life'.

name: Blessing
reference: Genesis 12:2 — God promises to bless Abraham and make him a blessing.

name: Trinity
reference: Named for the Holy Trinity, the Christian teaching of one God in three persons.

name: Evangeline
reference: From the Greek word for 'good news', the root of 'Gospel'.

name: Angelina
reference: From 'angel', the messengers of God throughout the Bible.

name: Angela
reference: Saint Angela Merici, founder of the Ursulines.

name: Christina
reference: Saint Christina, an early martyr.

name: Theodora
reference: Saint Theodora, an early martyr; several saints bear the name.

name: Dorothy
reference: Saint Dorothy of Caesarea, a young martyr.

name: Agnes
reference: Saint Agnes, a young Roman martyr.

name: Agatha
reference: Saint Agatha of Sicily, a martyr of the 3rd century.

name: Anastasia
reference: Saint Anastasia, an early martyr honored in East and West.

name: Bernadette
reference: Saint Bernadette of Lourdes, to whom Mary appeared in 1858.

name: Bridget
reference: Saint Brigid of Kildare, one of the patron saints of Ireland.

name: Catherine
reference: Saint Catherine of Alexandria and Saint Catherine of Siena.

name: Cecilia
reference: Saint Cecilia, the patron saint of music.

name: Clare
reference: Saint Clare of Assisi, a friend of Saint Francis.

name: Clara
reference: A Latin form of Clare, after Saint Clare of Assisi.

name: Helena
reference: Saint Helena, the mother of Emperor Constantine.

name: Elena
reference: A Spanish and Italian form of Helena, after Saint Helena.

name: Frances
reference: Saint Frances of Rome and the feminine form of Francis.

name: Gertrude
reference: Saint Gertrude the Great, a medieval mystic and writer.

name: Joan
reference: Saint Joan of Arc, the young French heroine and martyr.

name: Lucy
reference: Saint Lucy of Syracuse, a martyr whose feast day celebrates light.

name: Lucia
reference: The Latin and Italian form of Lucy, after Saint Lucy.

name: Margaret
reference: Saint Margaret of Antioch and Saint Margaret of Scotland.

name: Monica
reference: Saint Monica, the mother of Saint Augustine, known for her prayers.

name: Perpetua
reference: Saint Perpetua, a young martyr of Carthage in the 3rd century.

name: Rita
reference: Saint Rita of Cascia, known as a patron of hopeless causes.

name: Rose
reference: Saint Rose of Lima, the first canonized saint of the Americas.

name: Teresa
reference: Saint Teresa of Avila and Saint Teresa of Calcutta.

name: Veronica
reference: Saint Veronica, who by tradition wiped the face of Jesus on the road to Calvary.

name: Victoria
reference: Saint Victoria, an early martyr.

name: Ursula
reference: Saint Ursula, a legendary martyr honored across Europe.

name: Hildegard
reference: Saint Hildegard of Bingen, a medieval abbess, composer and writer.

name: Edith
reference: Saint Edith Stein, a philosopher and martyr; also Saint Edith of Wilton.

name: Louise
reference: Saint Louise de Marillac, who served the poor and sick.

name: Sophia
reference: Wisdom is praised throughout Proverbs; also Saint Sophia and her daughters.

name: Zoe
reference: Saint Zoe of Rome, an early martyr; 'zoe' is the Greek word for life in the Gospels.

name: Beatrice
reference: Saint Beatrice, an early Roman martyr.

name: Thecla
reference: Saint Thecla, remembered in early tradition as a follower of Paul.

name: Marcella
reference: Saint Marcella of Rome, a devoted student of Scripture.

name: Paula
reference: Saint Paula of Rome, a friend and coworker of Saint Jerome.

name: Eulalia
reference: Saint Eulalia of Barcelona, a young martyr.

name: Justina
reference: Saint Justina of Padua, an early martyr.

name: Petra
reference: A feminine form of Peter, the rock of Matthew 16:18.

name: Philippa
reference: A feminine form of Philip; see Acts 21:9 for Philip's prophesying daughters.

name: Stephanie
reference: A feminine form of Stephen, the first Christian martyr (Acts 6–7).

name: Alexandra
reference: A feminine form of Alexander; Saint Alexandra was an early martyr.

name: Andrea
reference: A feminine form of Andrew, the apostle (John 1:40).

name: Benedicta
reference: A feminine form of Benedict, after Saint Benedict of Nursia.

name: Clementine
reference: A feminine form of Clement, a coworker of Paul in Philippians 4:3.

name: Matilda
reference: Saint Matilda of Ringelheim, a queen known for her charity.

name: Natalie
reference: From the Latin for 'birthday', traditionally given to children born at Christmas.

name: Noelle
reference: The French word for Christmas, the celebration of Jesus' birth.

name: Epiphany
reference: The feast celebrating the visit of the Magi to Jesus (Matthew 2).

name: Pilar
reference: Named for Our Lady of the Pillar in Zaragoza, Spain.

name: Dolores
reference: Named for Our Lady of Sorrows, honoring Mary's grief at the cross.

name: Mercedes
reference: Named for Our Lady of Mercy, a Marian title.

name: Consuelo
reference: Named for Our Lady of Consolation, a Marian title.

name: Esperanza
reference: The Spanish word for hope, one of the three Christian virtues.

name: Rosario
reference: Named for Our Lady of the Rosary, a Marian title.

name: Celeste
reference: A name pointing to heaven, used among Christian families.

name: Seraphina
reference: From the seraphim, the angels who worship God in Isaiah 6:2.

name: Angelica
reference: From 'angel', the messengers of God throughout the Bible.

name: Pia
reference: The feminine form of Pius, a name borne by several popes.

name: Genevieve
meaning: Meaning debated; possibly 'woman of the race'
reference: Saint Genevieve, the patron saint of Paris.

name: Aurelia
reference: Saint Aurelia of Strasbourg, an early Christian woman.

name: Sabina
reference: Saint Sabina, a Roman martyr.

name: Flora
reference: Saint Flora of Córdoba, a 9th-century martyr.
